lines: An envelope generator that records a contour you draw with the mouse and plays it back down four lanes at different speeds, phases and loop settings, or works as a four-output ADSR
Fires every lane at once, and in ADSR mode fires a one-shot that reaches sustain and releases without a held gate
Cuts a quiet opening off the recorded gesture, treating anything under 1V for at least 25ms as silence and confirming 12ms of activity before the cut
Cuts the quiet stretch after the last active point off the recorded gesture and adds a return to 0V where one is needed
Steps the selected lane through Off, Forward, Reverse and Ping-Pong looping; in ADSR mode it is a plain on and off
Turns the selected lane's output upside down, so a 0-10V contour comes out running 10V to 0V and a bipolar one changes sign
Sets the playback speed of the selected lane, from 0.05 times to 8 times; in ADSR mode it sets the selected stage's time, or the sustain level
Offsets the selected lane through one whole turn of the gesture; in ADSR mode it bends the selected stage from logarithmic through linear to exponential
Selects which lane the shared speed, phase, loop and invert controls edit; in ADSR mode the four buttons select attack, decay, sustain and release instead
Switches between the recorded-gesture engine and a four-output ADSR envelope, keeping the gesture in the background while ADSR is chosen
A rising edge restarts that voice at the start of the gesture, or at the edge of its loop window; in ADSR mode it fires a one-shot that releases on its own
A rising edge starts a voice and a falling edge glides it down to 0V; in ADSR mode it runs the usual attack, sustain and release
Adds to that lane's phase offset, 10V being one whole turn of the gesture, and the result wraps round
Supplies a tempo for lanes set to a beat division, and never triggers anything; four rising edges establish the beat and only the first channel is read
That lane's envelope, 0-10V unless the menu sets it to 0-5V or bipolar
Carries 10V while that lane or ADSR voice is running
A 1ms pulse at 10V when that lane's one-shot finishes or it crosses the loop boundary its direction defines
Note — it does nothing until a gesture exists: click and hold on the touch strip and move up and down, high on the strip recording 10V and low recording 0V, up to five seconds
Note — starting a new recording stops all playback and replaces the stored gesture when it finishes; the gesture is saved with the patch
Note — with a lane looping, coloured start and end markers appear on the screen and can be dragged to narrow the part of the gesture that plays
Note — clicking the outlined capsule at the top of the screen cycles the selected lane between free running and a quarter, half, one, two or four beats of the clock input
Note — with both the trigger and the gate patched in gesture mode only the trigger is read; in ADSR mode both keep their own jobs
Note — a lane fitted to the clock ignores its speed setting until it is put back to free running
Note — putting a Recollect immediately to the right replaces the played contour with that module's two morphable memories, while recording, triggers and phase stay here
Note — the four per-lane speed CV inputs the manual describes are declared in the code but have no jack on the panel, so nothing can be patched to them
Menu — Gesture Mode — chooses the recorded-contour engine, the same choice the panel switch makes
Menu — ADSR Mode — chooses the four-output ADSR engine, the same choice the panel switch makes
Menu — Gesture trigger behavior — chooses whether a trigger restarts lanes that are already looping or leaves those loops running
Menu — Clock fit — sets each lane independently to free running or to a beat division of the clock input
Menu — Output voltage ranges — sets each lane's output independently to 0-10V, 0-5V or bipolar, and carries a normalize switch that scales the lane against the gesture's peak
Menu — Quantize ADSR Phase CV — is kept so old patches load, and changes nothing in this version because the ADSR contour has no CV path

Evocation.notes: Eleven parameters and four inputs are declared with no widget on the panel and can never be clicked: the four per-lane speed knobs, loop and invert for lanes two to four (the panel pair is shared and follows the selected lane), the two advance buttons, and the four speed CV inputs. The manual's Connections section lists SPEED 1-4 CV among the inputs, which is true of the code and not of the panel. The two large knobs are printed PARAM I and PARAM II on the panel; the manual calls them SPEED and PHASE.

lines: Two gesture memories for Evocation with separate transforms and a morph between them, and it goes immediately to the right of the Evocation it belongs to
Moves between the two transformed memories, all of A at the bottom and all of B at the top, crossfading matching points of the two contours
Low-pass smooths the selected memory in both directions at once, so hand jitter softens without the contour shifting earlier or later
Replaces the selected memory's detail with fewer straight segments, low settings keeping the hand and high settings leaving the geometry
Chooses which memory the next finished Evocation recording lands in, and which one the transform controls edit
Flips the selected memory in time before it is morphed, which is separate from Evocation's own loop direction
Folds the selected memory into the first half of its length and plays it back out through the second, so it ends where it started
Scales the selected transformed memory so its highest point reaches full
Adds to the morph knob, 10V covering the whole span from A to B and clamping at the ends; only the first channel is read
The transformed memory A on its own, 0-10V
The transformed memory B on its own, 0-10V
The current morph between the two transformed memories, 0-10V
Note — it shows AWAITING EVOCATION and does nothing until an Evocation is the module immediately to its left; a gap or another module between them breaks the link
Note — Evocation stays the performer: it records the gesture and supplies the triggers, loop direction, loop window, phase, clock fit and polyphony that these outputs follow
Note — a memory is written when a finished Evocation recording arrives, and by default the selector then moves to the other memory ready for the next take
Note — transforms never rewrite the stored take, so any of them can be changed or reset later
Note — the three jacks here are fixed at 0-10V and ignore Evocation's per-lane voltage range, invert and peak normalization
Note — it is inactive while Evocation is in ADSR mode, and both memories survive that
Menu — Alternate A/B after each capture — moves the record target to the other memory after each successful new take
Menu — Capture Evocation gesture — copies the gesture Evocation currently holds straight into the selected memory
Menu — Write protect — locks that memory against capture, clearing, copying into it and swapping, while leaving its transforms editable
Menu — Reset transforms — returns reverse, palindrome, smooth, simplify and normalize to neutral for the selected memory
Menu — Swap A and B — exchanges the two memories, and is refused unless both are unlocked
Menu — Clear — empties that memory
Menu — Show on screen — chooses which memory's source trace the screen draws

Recollect.notes: The panel and the code call the third transform PALINDROME and it folds the gesture out and back (recollect.cpp:463-476). The manual still lists a MIRROR transform that flips amplitude; the comment in the source says MIRROR was removed because it duplicated Evocation's own invert. The transforms are applied in the order reverse, palindrome, smooth, simplify, normalize.

lines: Two sigmoid oscillators with a pitch-locked formant modulator inside each waveform, crossfaded and spread across the stereo field, with cross sync and a reverse sync that can be made probabilistic
Tunes the V oscillator in whole octaves, two either way, and the menu can free it for a continuous sweep
Tunes the Z oscillator in semitones, two octaves either way, and the menu can free it for a continuous sweep
Detunes that oscillator by up to 20 cents either way
Sweeps that oscillator's sigmoid curve from a soft ramp to a sharp square-like edge, the morph finishing in roughly the first half of the travel; in PWM mode it sets the pulse width from 5% to 95%
Attenuates and inverts the shape jack for that oscillator before it moves the shape knob
Mixes the two oscillators at the output stage, all V at one end and all Z at the other
Attenuates and inverts the crossfade jack before it moves the crossfade knob
Makes the V oscillator reset the phase of the Z oscillator at each of its own cycles
Chooses the reverse sync: off, on, where each V cycle flips the direction the Z oscillator runs in, or mutual, where Z flips V in return
Sets how far the formant modulator bends the sigmoid curve inside each cycle; at zero the waveform is plain, and the character opens up from the middle of the travel upwards
Sets the formant modulator's speed as a multiple of the oscillator's own pitch, stepped through eight ratios from half up to seven
Skews the wave's symmetry, pouring even harmonics into an otherwise hollow symmetric wave; in PWM mode it skews the trajectory of the pulse-width modulation instead
Sets the stereo width from a true mono collapse at the bottom, through natural stereo at the middle, to twice that at the top, where the formant motion in the two channels runs fully out of phase
Attenuates and inverts the formant depth jack before it moves the depth knob
Attenuates and inverts the stereo width jack before it moves the width knob
Sets how often a reverse sync flip actually happens: every time at the top, and progressively at random below that
Attenuates and inverts the flip chance jack before it moves the chance knob
Sets the pitch of the V oscillator, a volt to the octave
Sets the pitch of the Z oscillator, a volt to the octave; unpatched it follows the V pitch jack, and a narrower polyphonic cable leaves the uncovered voices following their V partners
Moves the formant depth, 10V at full attenuation covering the whole range, and the total is clamped
Moves the stereo width, 10V at full attenuation sweeping the whole mono-to-wide range
Moves that oscillator's shape, and audio-rate signals are fair game here
Moves the crossfade between the two oscillators
Moves the reverse sync flip chance, 10V at full attenuation covering the whole range
The left channel of the pair
The right channel of the pair; for mono work take the left jack alone, or set the width to zero
Note — it makes sound as soon as it is added to a patch, with the formant section already at work; a pitch cable is an addition rather than a requirement
Note — the formant modulator tracks each oscillator's own pitch, so its character survives transposition; a nearly pure sawtooth gives it little to bend, so raise the shape knobs to the middle
Note — the voice count follows the widest cable patched to any input, and both outputs carry that count; each voice pairs channel n of one pitch jack with channel n of the other
Note — the screen draws either the left output against the right as a Lissajous figure or a triggered trace of the left output with the right ghosted behind it
Menu — Quantize — frees the V octave control or the Z semitone control, or both, for continuous sweeps in place of their stepped behaviour
Menu — Oscilloscope Display — chooses between the Lissajous plot of left against right and a triggered waveform trace
Menu — Waveform — chooses the morphing sigmoid sawtooth or a band-limited pulse wave, which changes what the shape, depth and asymmetry controls do
Menu — Crossfade Curve — chooses an equal-power blend or a stereo swap where the two oscillators cross the field and trade sides
Menu — Oversampling — sets the internal rate at 1, 2, 4 or 8 times, the higher settings costing processor time and cleaning up mutual reverse sync and fast shape modulation
Menu — Vintage — sets how much thermal drift, per-voice component tolerance, crosstalk and bus saturation the module shows, 50% being the calibrated amount
Menu — Oscillator Noise — adds a hardware-like noise floor and tiny phase jitter that softens the waveform edges

lines: Two morphing filters that can be separated in cutoff, cross-coupled into each other, routed four ways, and stirred by an internal chaotic modulator
Sets that filter's base cutoff, from 20Hz to about 20.5kHz, with extra travel given to the midrange
Sets that filter's resonant feedback, the upper part of the range crossing into stabilized self-oscillation
Copies filter A's cutoff to filter B and then moves both together from either knob
Copies filter A's resonance to filter B and then moves both together from either knob
Attenuates and inverts the cutoff jack beside it; with 1V per octave tracking chosen in the menu it becomes the tracking amount and direction instead
Attenuates and inverts the resonance jack beside it, 10V at full attenuation adding 1.0 to the raw resonance figure
Feeds each filter's previous output into the other, saturated and bounded before it returns; low settings tie the stereo movement together and high settings set up circulating harmonics
Scales how far the chaotic modulator moves the field
Morphs both filters continuously from a 6-pole lowpass at the bottom, through resonant bandpass at the middle, to a 2-pole highpass at the top
Sets the speed of the chaotic modulator, from 0.01Hz to 10Hz
Pulls filter A's cutoff down and filter B's up by equal amounts, three octaves apart in total at the top of its travel
The signal filter A works on; with only one of the two audio jacks patched it feeds both filters
The signal filter B works on; with only one of the two audio jacks patched it feeds both filters
Moves that filter's cutoff, scaled by the trimmer beside it; with 1V per octave tracking chosen in the menu it transposes the cutoff instead
Moves that filter's resonance, scaled by the trimmer beside it
Moves the cross-coupling, 10V covering the whole range, and each voice can have a different amount
Moves the chaotic modulation depth, 10V covering the whole range
Moves the filter shape from lowpass through bandpass to highpass, 10V covering the whole range
Adds to the chaotic modulator's rate at half a hertz a volt, clamped to the knob's own range; only the first channel is read
Adds to the cutoff separation, 10V adding the full three octaves; only the first channel is read
A gate at 1V or above holds the chaotic modulator in place while it lasts, without changing the latch set by clicking the screen
Filter A's output
Filter B's output
Note — with only one audio jack patched the same signal goes to both filters, which is the fastest way to hear the pair
Note — clicking anywhere on the screen latches both chaotic sources at their present values, and clicking again releases them from exactly where they stopped
Note — the voice count comes from the audio inputs alone, up to 16; a CV cable on its own creates no voices
Note — the first voice uses the exact cutoff settings and the rest get small fixed random offsets within about a semitone and a half, so the resonant peaks of a chord do not stack
Note — the screen draws the whole field as one figure rather than two response curves: coupling twists the orbit, spread separates its bands, and the routing changes its direction
Menu — Screen particles — chooses a brighter image that flickers at its hottest points or a steadier, softer one, and changes nothing in the audio
Menu — Filter routing — chooses Parallel stereo, either serial order, or Mid / Side, where A filters the middle and B the sides
Menu — Opposed Form (reverse B) — runs filter B backwards through the shape morph, so one is lowpass while the other is highpass and they meet at bandpass
Menu — Chaos destination — chooses whether the chaotic modulator moves only the cutoffs, the cutoffs and resonance, or the whole field including shape and coupling
Menu — Filter character: Still, Liquid, Volatile — chooses whether the level-dependent movement is removed, calibrated, or exaggerated
Menu — Freeze chaos field — latches the chaotic modulator at its present values, which clicking the screen also does
Menu — Filter A 1V/oct tracking — turns filter A's cutoff jack from plain modulation into pitch tracking, with the trimmer setting how much and which way
Menu — Filter B 1V/oct tracking — turns filter B's cutoff jack from plain modulation into pitch tracking, with the trimmer setting how much and which way

lines: A polyphonic stereo amplifier in front of a five-algorithm distortion engine, with level-matching between the clean and distorted paths and a sidechain input that can open, duck or drive the dirt
Sets the clean signal level, from silence to unity, before the distortion engine
Chooses the distortion algorithm: hard clip, tube sat, wave fold, bit crush or ring mod, crossfaded over 12ms when it changes
Opens the chosen algorithm and sets how far it goes, which is the fold count, the bit depth and hold, or the ring modulator's carrier depending on the algorithm
Attenuates and inverts the jack below it before it is added to the control it belongs to
Adds gain into the distorted path alone, setting how hard the amplified signal strikes the chosen circuit
Crossfades from the clean amplified signal to the level-matched distorted one
Replaces the right input with the left, which matters when a right cable is patched and should be overridden
Chooses whether the amplifier's control is taken as it is or squared, the squared setting opening more sharply and reaching four times gain under voltage
Ties the distortion depth to how loud the signal already is: centred is off, one way dirties loud passages and leaves quiet ones clean, the other way reverses that, per voice
Splits the distortion depth between the two sides, centred being off and either direction making one side dirtier by up to half the distortion range
The left channel in, which also feeds the right when the right jack is empty
The right channel in; with this patched and the left empty, nothing comes out
Sets the amplifier gain per voice, 10V adding one whole unit of gain, so one polyphonic envelope can articulate a chord
Detects how far a signal swings from zero and drives whichever sidechain behaviour the menu has chosen; a bipolar audio signal and a 0-10V envelope both reach the top of its range
Steps the distortion algorithm on, 0-10V running through the five types from the first and pinning at the last; only the first channel is read
Moves the distortion amount, scaled by the trimmer above it; only the first channel is read
Moves the drive, scaled by the trimmer above it; only the first channel is read
Moves the wet and dry blend, scaled by the trimmer above it; only the first channel is read
Moves the contrast setting over its whole bipolar span with no trimmer, so a bipolar source sweeps it end to end from the centre; only the first channel is read
Moves the stereo tilt over its whole bipolar span with no trimmer, so a bipolar source sweeps it end to end from the centre; only the first channel is read
The left channel out
The right channel out
Note — a new module comes up with the amplifier closed, so silence is what to expect until the gain knob is raised
Note — with the distortion amount or the mix at zero the nonlinear engines are skipped entirely, which is where most of the processor cost goes at high voice counts
Note — the distorted path is level-matched against the clean one before the mix, so moving from dry to ruined is not also a move from quiet to loud
Note — the voice count is the wider of the two audio inputs, up to 16; control cables create no voices
Note — the output is linear through ordinary levels and then enters a soft knee, approaching a ceiling rather than clipping abruptly
Menu — Oversampling — sets the internal rate at 1, 2, 4 or 8 times; it is tonal as well as a processor cost, and the wave folder changes most
Menu — Enhancement (Trigger) — makes the sidechain scale the distortion and drive up from zero to their settings, holding the mix at 80% wet or above
Menu — Ducking (Inverse) — makes a hot sidechain cut the distortion and back off the drive
Menu — Direct Control — makes the sidechain replace the distortion amount and its CV, leaving drive and mix working as usual
Menu — Duck Level (classic) — makes a hot sidechain turn the amplifier down, to about a tenth at full, which also softens how hard the signal hits the distortion

lines: Two peak meters with VU-style dials and mechanical needle movement, passing every sample straight through while they watch
The signal that side meters, passed to the output beside it unchanged
An exact copy of the input for that side, with the same channel count and no gain, filtering or delay
Note — the two sides are independent and nothing is normalled between them, so patching the left alone leaves the right meter at rest and its output empty
Note — the dial runs from -20 VU to +3 VU, where 0 VU is about 7.08V peak and +3 VU is the 10V peak that is full scale in Rack, so the red half of the dial is the last 3dB of headroom
Note — the needle rises with a 15ms time constant and falls with a 450ms one, which reveals a transient without vibrating too fast to read
Note — with a polyphonic cable the dial follows the loudest channel present, so one hot voice cannot hide inside a chord
Note — the detector reads absolute magnitude, so a slow control voltage moves the needle the same way whether it goes positive or negative
Menu — Screen brightness — sets how brightly the dials are lit, which changes the artwork alone and not the needles or the signal

lines: A blank panel that can be resized from 2HP to 64HP by dragging either edge, keeping its leather grain at a fixed scale and saving its width with the patch
Note — a narrow strip along each edge is the resize handle: drag the right edge to move the right boundary and the left edge to move the left one, and the width rounds to whole HP
Note — a newly added panel arrives at 2HP and looks for the nearest modules on its row, expanding to fill a bounded gap; one loaded from a patch keeps its saved width instead
Note — double-clicking the panel or either resize edge measures the surrounding gap again, which is what to do after the neighbouring modules move
Note — Rack checks for collisions, so a width or position it cannot accept returns the panel to where it was
Menu — Fit to surrounding gap — measures from the nearest module ending on the left to the nearest beginning on the right and fills that space, capped at 64HP
UtilityPanel.notes: The module has no parameters, inputs or outputs. Auto-fit needs a module bounding the right side; an open-ended row leaves the panel unchanged.
